extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal financial assistance (K-12 and postsecondary institutions), Title IX coordinators, higher-education administrators, legal counsel, compliance officers
extracted.subtask_short: Title IX recipient sexual harassment response
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for institutions on when and how recipients must respond to sexual harassment under Title IX, and how those obligations interact with the Clery Act, FERPA, and institutional conduct processes. Covers definitions (education program or activity), emergency removals, advisors/cross-examination, standards of evidence, and geographic scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic scope: Title IX vs. Clery Act
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX prohibits discrimination on the basis of sex against 'a person in the United States.' The Clery Act requires reporting of crimes that occur on Clery geography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The only specific geographic limitation in Title IX is that the sex discrimination must be against a person in the United States. Title IX may require a recipient to respond to incidents that occur off campus if those incidents occur in the recipient's education program or activity; Clery's geographic reporting obligations are distinct and do not by themselves determine Title IX obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'education program or activity' (§106.44(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: For the purposes of §§106.30, 106.44, and 106.45, 'education program or activity' includes locations, events, or circumstances over which the recipient exercised substantial control over both the respondent and the context in which the harassment occurs, and also includes any building owned or controlled by a student organization that is officially recognized by a postsecondary institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determinations of whether conduct falls within an institution's education program or activity require fact-specific analysis of control and relationships (including recognized student organization buildings, on- and off-campus).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient duty upon actual knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recipient has actual knowledge of sexual harassment in its education program or activity against a person in the United States, the recipient must respond promptly and in a manner that is not deliberately indifferent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This duty applies irrespective of whether the harassment occurs on or off campus so long as it is within the recipient's education program or activity; the Department will enforce the obligation to avoid deliberate indifference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory dismissal of formal complaints (§106.45(b)(3)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: The institution must dismiss an allegation of sexual harassment in a formal complaint in certain circumstances as specified in §106.45(b)(3)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A dismissal under these Title IX regulations does not preclude the recipient from addressing the same conduct under other provisions of the institution's code of conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency removal (§106.44(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may remove a respondent from its education program or activity on an emergency basis after conducting an individualized safety and risk analysis that determines an immediate threat to the physical health or safety of any student or other individual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions have discretion who conducts the analysis and who hears any immediate post-removal challenge, must provide notice and an opportunity to challenge immediately following removal, may remove from some or all programs, and the Department will defer to the recipient's decision provided it is not deliberately indifferent. This emergency removal process is separate from Clery Act timely-warning/notification processes and need not use the same analytical procedures as Clery or FERPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely warnings and Clery Act notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether an institution needs to issue a timely warning is governed by the regulations implementing the Clery Act and its conditions (e.g., Clery crime, Clery geography).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title IX emergency removal does not automatically require a Clery Act emergency notification; institutions may validly reach different determinations about emergency removal versus issuing a timely warning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisor of choice: status and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: An advisor may be, but is not required to be, an attorney. Institutions are not required to provide legal representation for parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions must permit parties to have an advisor of their choice present, but are not required to provide one; they may establish rules governing advisor conduct as long as rules are applied equally to both parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisor role and cross-examination at postsecondary live hearings (§106.45(b)(6)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: For postsecondary institution recipients, the regulations require a live hearing and permit cross-examination by a party's advisor; the advisor may be, but is not required to be, an attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions must provide an advisor for the limited purpose of conducting cross-examination at the hearing (or allow the party to have an advisor who conducts cross-examination). Institutions may train advisors and may prevent disruptive conduct, but must afford both parties the same opportunities regarding advisors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on advisor participation (Clery/Title IX consistency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clery Act regulations permit institutions to establish restrictions on the extent to which an advisor may participate in proceedings so long as the restriction applies to both parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title IX regulations contain similar language but require provision of an advisor for cross-examination at postsecondary hearings; restrictions on advisor participation must be equally applied and may address disruptive behavior or orderly conduct rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may adopt either the preponderance of the evidence standard or the clear and convincing evidence standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The only requirement is that the recipient use the same standard of evidence for complaints against students as it does for complaints against employees (including faculty). The Department does not emphasize one standard over the other and is not requiring alignment with civil litigation evidentiary rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction of Clery reporting and Title IX obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions may be required under the Clery Act to report certain incidents (e.g., dating violence, domestic violence, stalking, sexual assault) that occur in certain off-campus locations and to notify victims of rights, but Title IX grievance requirements and dismissal rules are not identical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting incidents under Clery (and thus having actual knowledge) does not automatically obligate Title IX formal investigation if the incident falls outside the Title IX definition or must be dismissed under Title IX rules; institutions can still address conduct under other institutional policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Greek-letter organizations and recognized student organization buildings
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Greek letter organization housing counts as part of a recipient's education program or activity depends on the relationship between the recipient and the organization; §106.44(a) includes buildings owned or controlled by an officially recognized student organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This Title IX test may include certain off-campus fraternity/sorority properties that Clery's noncampus property definition would exclude; institutions should evaluate recognition and control relationships when determining obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of application to elementary and secondary schools
rubrics_metrics.description: Elementary and secondary schools historically have not been subject to Clery Act geographic requirements; imposing Clery geography obligations on recipients of Federal financial assistance (generally K-12) is inappropriate given differences in scope and student mobility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title IX's geographic limitation is that prohibited discrimination is against a person in the United States; institutions should not conflate Clery reporting geography with Title IX coverage for K-12 contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department deference to recipient procedural choices
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department defers to recipients on many procedural choices (who conducts emergency removal risk assessments, who hears challenges, whether to remove from all programs or some, whether to use the §106.45 grievance process for emergency removals), subject to the requirement not to be deliberately indifferent and to avoid conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As long as recipients provide required notices, opportunity to challenge, avoid conflicts of interest (see §106.45(b)(1)(iii)), and are not deliberately indifferent, the Department will not second-guess reasonable institutional decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption/adaptation of Supreme Court framework (Gebser and Davis)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department is adopting and adapting the rubric in the Supreme Court's decisions in Gebser and Davis to administer Title IX requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This framework underpins the Department's approach to recipient liability and obligations in responding to sexual harassment under Title IX.
